question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=80$ from a population where $70%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that between $60%$ and $80%$ of the sample have the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=80,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.7.$

Now, since

$$
np=80(0.7)=56>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=80(1-0.7)=24>5,
$$

and $n=80$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.7,\frac{0.7(1-0.7)}{80}) \\  & ∼N(0.7,0.002\,625).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.6\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.8).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.6\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.8) & =P(\frac{0.6-0.7}{\sqrt{0.002\,625}}\le Z\le \frac{0.8-0.7}{\sqrt{0.002\,625}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.95\le Z\le 1.95) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.95)-P(Z\le -1.95) \\  & =Φ(1.95)-Φ(-1.95)\end{aligned}
$$
